subject.title: Memory search: bound primary embeddings before the outer tool deadline and fall back to FTS

question: Should OpenClaw add a documented internal primary-embedding budget that falls back to indexed FTS results, or retain the current single outer-deadline/provider-fallback behavior?
rationale: The report asks for a new timeout boundary and potentially a new configuration surface that changes when users receive semantic versus lexical recall; source-level confirmation is still needed before choosing the durable contract.

options.title: Adopt bounded FTS fallback
options.body: Specify an internal primary-embedding budget and return explicitly lexical FTS results when that budget expires, while preserving caller aborts.

options.title: Keep one deadline
options.body: Retain the existing deadline and provider fallback behavior, documenting or tuning the existing timeout path instead of adding a lexical fallback policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt bounded FTS fallback
recommendation.body: Specify an internal primary-embedding budget and return explicitly lexical FTS results when that budget expires, while preserving caller aborts.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent work is the closest available history signal for memory embedding-provider behavior, though ownership should be verified from the affected plugin history.
